# 08-fresco — sources

Back-test entry `08-fresco.yaml`: Fresco, the AI scribe for construction superintendents (YC Fall 2024).
Written 2026-10-22 from public material only. Quotes are verbatim from the page named; "Author's choice" marks the
smallest plausible choice made where the public material is silent.

Main sources:
- [HN] Launch HN: Fresco (YC F24), 2024-11-21 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42204939
- [LYC] Launch YC: Fresco, the scribe for construction, 2024-10-23 — https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/M73-fresco-the-scribe-for-construction
- [YCP] YC company page — https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fresco (now "AI-powered takeoff and estimating for Division 8 construction")
- [KOE] A contractor's daily-log expectations on Procore's support site — https://support.procore.com/tc/Koester/Site_Map/Koester_Expectations_-_Daily_Logs
- [SWI] Swiftask, Procore daily reports page (vendor) — https://swiftask.ai/ai-integration/procore/intelligent-daily-reports
- [BLS] BLS Occupational Outlook, construction managers — https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/construction-managers.htm
- [OPU] Launch HN: Opusense (field reports for site inspectors), 2025-05-20 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44042791

## The eight founder-emulation items

1. **Who.** Construction superintendents on commercial jobs.
   [HN] "Superintendents are the busiest and most expensive people on construction sites."
   [LYC] "That’s the reality for 210k+ construction superintendents (or supervisors, foremen, PMs, etc.) across the USA."
   → `roles[superintendent]`, `context.actor`, `actor_plural`. Author's choice: "on commercial jobs" (the founders ask
   for introductions to commercial general contractors in [LYC]).

2. **What (the job).** Keep the record of the day's work, for liability and disputes.
   [HN] "30-200 photos per day to document site progress (mostly for liability reasons, or in case of a dispute with the
   owner over delays and deliverables)"; photos used to create "daily logs", "structured documents that account for the
   work done on site on any given day". [KOE] the log is "a critical piece of documentation in the arbitration of a
   dispute". → `statements.problem`, `context.job`, `interpretations.problem`.

3. **When / where.** At the end of the day, after the site walks, in the trailer.
   [HN] "At the end of the day, they'll spend a few hours uploading those photos into OneDrive, or project management
   software like Procore or ACC." [YCP] "We were curious what superintendents were doing for hours in their trailers at
   the end of the day." [LYC] "supes are spending up to 3 hours a day creating documents". → `context.circumstance`, `occasion: daily log`.
   Author's choice: the recall window {5, WORKING_DAYS} and Frequency 4 to 5 working days out of 5 (the posts say "per
   day"; a five-day site week is assumed). Prevalence `p_80_100` ("Nearly all") follows from the same "per day".

4. **Which people (the comparable group).** Superintendents at US general contractors whose jobs run on Procore or ACC.
   [LYC] "210k+ construction superintendents ... across the USA"; "Project management tools like Procore and ACC have
   dramatically increased documentation requirements". [YCP] "driving to Napa, South Bay, and around SF". → `context.segment`,
   `market: US`.

5. **Who pays.** The general contractor, per site.
   [HN] "we charge per site per month, which includes unlimited users on any given construction project".
   → `persona.decision_maker: {role: contractor}`, the BUYER role. Author's choice: the decider is the contractor's
   "operations lead" and the role to test is "The CFO" (a second role, "The project executive", listed); Purchase
   friction's three steps ("A trial on one live job" tested, a Procore check, a security review) and Commitment's step
   "start a paid pilot on one site" are the author's. Public material names no buyer title; [LYC] asks for
   introductions to general contractors by firm, not by role.

6. **Mechanism.** Narrated short videos turned into notes, texted to the crew, pushed to Procore/ACC.
   [HN] "Supers simply take short videos with voiceover, or upload photos, and Fresco does the rest, creating notes with
   transcription, photos, assignees, and due dates. Supers can easily text their crew action items, and receive texts
   back". "We also route this to whatever project management software they're using with a single click."
   [LYC] the narrated example "The beam in the southwest corner of room 134 is corroded and needs replacement by Alex.";
   "Supes who use Fresco complete their notes, on average, 90% faster."
   → `statements.solution`, `solution_mechanism`, Compatibility and Adoption friction items. Relative advantage's two
   benefits are from [HN] ("during their site walks, not after") and [LYC] ("90% faster"); their wording is the author's.

7. **Price.** About $1k per site per month, less with multi-site or multi-month terms.
   [HN] "The typical price is $1k/month, but we offer discounts for multi-month or multi-site commitments."
   → `commercial.price` {800, 1000, month}. Author's choice: the low end of $800 stands for the stated discounts.
   Existing sacrifice: 30 to 60 hours a month per site at an hourly rate of 55 — from [LYC] "up to 3 hours a day" and
   [HN] "a few hours uploading", taken as 1.5 to 3 hours on about twenty working days (author's arithmetic). The rate is
   [BLS] "$55.28 per hour" (median, construction managers, May 2025), the author's stand-in: no superintendent wage is
   in the public material. Ability to pay is derived by code (24% to 61%).

8. **Occasions.** The narrated beam; a school refit report; the uploads and logs at the end of the day.
   [LYC] on a school refit walkthrough: "Normally, creating the final report takes 2+ hours."
   [HN] "few supers have time to do this thoroughly, so these photos aren't very searchable." No named customer quote
   exists in public; the occasions below are scripted from these and from practitioner comments.

No respondent carries the name of a commenter, customer or founder.

## Open
- The verdict was scripted to be plausible and not obviously "build": the problem holds on how often but people
  disagree on whether the log is one of their two worst difficulties; the solution splits on the benefit and on
  talking over videos on site; the price fails (two of eight at the founder's band or above) while the cost it would
  replace is above the price. This is the author's reading of the thread's sceptics, not a measured result.
- No public account names a buyer title at a general contractor; the decider, the tested role "The CFO", the purchase
  steps and the Commitment step are the author's.
- hourly_rate 55 is a proxy (construction managers, not superintendents).
- Existing sacrifice picks use `period: quarter` (the corpus's convention), although the registry's recall period for a
  monthly cost reads "last month"; the values are the monthly figures times three.
- The window {5, WORKING_DAYS} is the author's; the public posts say "per day".

insights.line: What made the others more pressing?

whys.g1: Both answers say the schedule and subs not showing up is what beats the log, so one group named in plain site language is exactly how a super would sort them.
whys.g2: There is no junk on this line, since both answers are on-topic and say what made the other problems more pressing.

founder.order_why: It runs from naming and market to context, then the problem's size, frequency, other difficulties and current workaround, then who asks and who gets the link, which is how I'd explain Fresco to someone new.
founder.asked_twice: Screens 3 and 5 carry the same question ('Before we test anything, let's define exactly where this idea applies.') on either side of the recency screen, so the context step reads as if it is asked twice, unless screen 5 is plainly a review of what screen 3 set.
founder.missing: There is nothing on the solution or the money side of Fresco: the mechanism (narrated short videos and photos turned into notes with assignees and due dates, texted to the crew, pushed to Procore/ACC in one click), the price ($1k per site per month, less with multi-site or multi-month terms), and the buyer (the general contractor pays per site, not the superintendent). Without these, the study tests only the problem. Screen 12 also has a typo: 'rcord' should be 'record'.

PRIMARY.order_why: It goes from whether I'm on Procore, to whether and how often the log ate hours, to what I'd want easier, then to the photo upload itself, which is how my day actually runs. The only snag is that screens 1 and 2 both say '1 of 4'.
PRIMARY.asked_twice: Screens 2 and 3 cover nearly the same ground (did I spend hours typing up the log, then on how many days), though 3 does follow up on 2.
PRIMARY.missing: How long the photo upload into Procore actually takes compared with the typing, and whether I've had to go back to my logs later, like pulling them for a delay dispute with the owner.

screens.why4: Named people, a Keel-found list and an open link posted where supers already gather (a superintendents' group or forum) cover the real ways I'd reach them and don't overlap.
screens.why5: Nothing of my idea is restated or bent here, and nothing about Fresco, Procore or the CFO role leaks into what a respondent would receive.
screens.instead: Who gets a link? — People I know by name (I send each their own link) / People Keel finds for me (Keel builds the list; I send each link) / A group I'm already in (one open link I post there; each person signs in with Google)

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' is stated, but the headline names only Frequency with '4 answered'. It omits the 5 needed and that Importance and Current solution stalled the same way, so I have to go to the cards to see what decides it.
screens.why_b2: The tally and each card's 'N answered · 5 needed' are plain, but 7 people answered and only 4 counted on three cards, and the page never says why the other 3 dropped out, so I had to look twice.
screens.why_b3: The Importance and Current solution lines are word for word the beliefs I checked, and the dimension names are the ones I saw going in.
screens.why_b4: '5 needed to call it' hints that I need at least one more superintendent through the study, but the page never says so, or what Prevalence holding means for Fresco.
screens.why_b5: With only 7 people, it refuses to call three beliefs and marks Prevalence as held only 'at the bar' at 6 of 7, so it claims nothing the answers can't carry.
screens.instead: Too few to call: only 4 of my 7 superintendents got through Frequency, Importance and Current solution (5 needed, and say why 3 didn't count). Prevalence held, just, at 6 of 7. Get at least one more super through the whole study before reading the problem.

screens.why_b1: "Holding up" sits right beside "6 of 7 said yes · bar 6 of 7 · at the bar", so I see both the verdict and the number that decides it, and they agree (6 of 7 is about 86%, just over my 8 in 10).
screens.why_b2: The strip shows 7 cells on a 0 to 7 axis, 6 for and 1 against, with my bar marked at 6, so what is counted, over how many and where the bar sits read at a glance.
screens.why_b3: Prevalence is my dimension and "8 in 10" is my band, but the line says "spent hours typing up their daily log" where I wrote uploading the day's photos and typing the log, so it's recognisable but narrower and leans on "hours".
screens.why_b4: "Common among these 7, at your bar exactly" plus a pointer to the next two cards is honest, but it doesn't say what this means for Fresco, e.g. that the occasion is there and the real test is whether it ranks.
screens.why_b5: n=7 is on the screen, the small group is called "a lean, not a call", and "at your bar exactly" keeps it from sounding stronger than 6 of 7 is.
screens.instead: Holding up, just: 6 of 7 supers spent hours on the photos and daily log last week, and the one no was between jobs. The occasion is there; whether it's one of their two worst is the card that decides.

screens.why_b1: The status 'Too few to call' sits beside its number, but the headline says '4 answered' while the count line says '6 answered · 4 counted', so I have to work out that 4 means counted, not answered.
screens.why_b2: The caption and the strip make clear it counts working days out of 5 and that the bar is 3 of 4, but the legend 'what you said at what you said short of it' runs its labels together and needs a second look.
screens.why_b3: Frequency and '4 to 5 working days out of 5' are what I checked, and 'spend hours typing up their daily log' is my trade's wording for the trailer work.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic; it doesn't say that all four counted are inside my range and that one more counted answer would decide it.
screens.why_b5: The low n is stated and nothing is called strong, but labelling 4 counted as '4 answered' understates who replied, and Hank's row repeats 'would rather not say' twice.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 6 answered, 4 counted (Hank declined, Luis guessed); all 4 put it at 4 to 5 days, middle answer 5. One more counted answer decides it, so ask another super about last week.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits beside '4 answered · 5 needed', but that line says 4 answered while the count line says 6 answered and 4 counted, so the deciding number contradicts itself, and nothing says that 2 of 4 is already below the 3 of 4 bar.
screens.why_b2: The bars count picks (8) but the bar is set in people (3 of 4), and the strip shows 8 cells (2 for, 6 against) although it is meant to be one cell a person, so I had to look twice to see that only 2 people counted against me, not 6.
screens.why_b3: Importance, with my belief word for word: daily logs and photos as one of the two of five they would most like made easier.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic: it doesn't say I need one more counted superintendent, or that the result leans against me because the two who didn't pick it named schedule and subs.
screens.why_b5: The low n is stated plainly, but the 6-against strip makes the opposition look three times larger than the 2 people it is, and 'a lean, not a call' never says which way it leans.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 4 of 6 counted (5 needed); 2 of 4 put the log in their two, under the 3-of-4 bar, and the other two put schedule and subs first. Get at least one more counted answer before believing either way.

screens.why_b1: Too few to call is stated with 4 and 5 needed beside it, but the header says 4 answered while the count line says 6 answered and 4 counted, so the deciding number disagrees with itself.
screens.why_b2: Who is counted and the line are plain, but the bar label reads 3 of 4, which looks like my result rather than the bar, and the ghost cell needs a second look to read as the one more answer needed.
screens.why_b3: The title and the belief line are the ones I checked on the way in, word for word.
screens.why_b4: Nothing is settled here yet is generic; it does not say that 3 of 4 already lean my way and that one more counted superintendent would settle it.
screens.why_b5: It claims nothing beyond the data and says a small group is a lean, not a call, but the header's 4 answered misstates the 6 who actually answered.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 6 answered, 4 counted (Hank declined, Luis guessed); 3 of 4 lean your way, so one more counted answer would decide it.

screens.why_b1: The status word 'Too few to call' sits directly above '4 answered · 5 needed to call it', so I know the verdict and the number that decides it.
screens.why_b3: 'Importance' and the belief line about logs and photos being one of the two things they most want made easier are exactly what I checked.
screens.why_b4: '5 needed to call it' implies I need one more answer, but nothing says what two of four ranking schedule and subs above the log means for Fresco. The screen is also silent on why Current solution, which I also checked, has no box.
screens.why_b5: The n of 4 and the 2 against stay visible, the low n is said outright, and nothing is called strong or held.
screens.why_b6: I did not type that schedule slippage and no-show subs beat the log, nor that one super already finishes it on a tablet before leaving the gate; both sharpen who Fresco is for and what it competes with.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 2 of 4 put schedule and subs above the log, so get at least one more answer before deciding; also say why Current solution shows no whys here.

screens.why1: Checking first whether I run a job on Procore or ACC makes sense before asking about my daily logs, since that's who this is for.
screens.why2: Procore and ACC are the tools I and every super I know use; nothing here I'd have to read twice.
screens.why3: I know exactly what platform each of my jobs is on, so I can answer straight off.
screens.why4: Yes or no covers it cleanly, and a screener needs no escape.
screens.why5: It asks only about the platform, which is the founder's segment, and nothing about their product slips through.
screens.why6: The question says fine, and ACC is spoken as letters on site anyway, but "I'll read 2 options. Yes; or No." is a mouthful for a yes-or-no; the screener's own form, "Yes or no," says it better.
screens.instead: Is any job you run now on Procore or ACC? Yes or no.

screens.why1: Right after asking if I run a job on Procore or ACC, it makes sense to check whether I actually did a daily log this week before asking for the story of one.
screens.why2: Two questions are packed into one: did I do a log, and did it take hours. I fill the log in most days, but some days it's 30 minutes, so I'd stop and wonder whether to say yes or no.
screens.why3: Putting the day's photos and notes into the daily log is my job every working day, so I can answer this from last week.
screens.why4: Yes and No are fine for a gate, but it has two escape chips where a gate should have none: 'I'd rather not say' isn't an allowed escape, and 'I can't recall one particular daily log' makes no sense on a yes-or-no about the last five days.
screens.why5: 'Spend hours' writes the founder's assumed pain into the screening question, so a super whose log was quick gets screened out, and I can tell what answer they're hoping for.
screens.why6: Said aloud it's short and is one question I can answer on hearing it, ending 'Yes or no.' with nothing extra read out.
screens.instead: In the last 5 working days, did you put together a daily log for one of your jobs? Yes or no. (no escape chips)

screens.why1: I just said yes to spending hours on the log this week, so asking how many of the five days that happened is the obvious next question.
screens.why2: Daily log, five working days, typing it up: those are my words, and I can count the days straight off.
screens.why3: I fill out the Procore daily log every night, so I know exactly which days it ate my evening.
screens.why4: One to five covers every answer after a yes, there's no overlap, and 'I can't recall' fits a count like this.
screens.why5: My time goes into getting the photos and the walk notes into the log, not just the typing, so 'typing up' narrows it a little, and 'hours' sets a bar where an hour-long day is hard to place.
screens.why6: It's one short question, and 'a number from 1 to 5' with the single escape is easy to hold and answer out loud.
screens.instead: In the last 5 working days, on how many days did getting your photos and notes into the daily log take an hour or more? 1 · 2 · 3 · 4 · 5 · I can't recall

screens.why1: After asking whether and how often I spent hours on the log, asking which part of my week I'd most like made easier is the obvious next step.
screens.why2: RFIs, submittals, subs and daily logs are words I use every day, and I can answer it on first read.
screens.why3: All five are things I fought with last week on my own job, so I can pick one from what I actually did.
screens.why4: Getting subs to show up and finish is most of what keeping the job on schedule means to me, so those two overlap; and I don't type up photos, I upload them.
screens.why5: The daily log option sits among the other headaches as just one of five, and nothing about a product or anybody's app reaches me.
screens.why6: It's one short question with five short options I can hold in my head, and 'none of these' comes last.
screens.instead: Think of your last week on site. Which one of these would you most like made easier? Keeping the job on schedule · Chasing RFIs and submittals · Keeping the site safe · Getting the daily log and photos in · Dealing with the owner and inspectors · None of these

screens.why1: Asking how my last log went fits after picking what I'd most like made easier, but screen 3 already had me count the days I spent hours on it, so this half-repeats that.
screens.why2: Taking site photos and uploading them is plain to me, but 'how did it go' is vague, and the options then talk about the log, not the photos, so I'd have to read it twice.
screens.why3: I take the photos on every walk and push them to Procore every day, so I know exactly how my last one went.
screens.why4: The stem asks about the photos and uploading, but the options say where and when the log got written, so my real answer is missing ('the upload dragged', 'I had to sort and caption them all after'); the escape should be the one for this dimension, not 'I can't recall'.
screens.why5: The pain of photos all day and hours uploading to Procore is still there in the stem, but the options drift to log timing, and nothing of the product leaks.
screens.why6: Five short options I can hold, but the stem packs two acts into one breath ('taking, then uploading'), and 'Log done on site' sounds clipped heard next to the rest.
screens.instead: Think of your last daily log. How long did getting the day's photos into Procore take? Under 15 minutes · 15 minutes to under an hour · 1 to under 2 hours · 2 hours or more · I didn't get them all in; escape: I can't recall

typo_leaks.text: How do construction superintendents keep an accurate rcord of the day's work on site today?
